1 Principles governing stop and search

1.1 Powers to stop and search must be used fairly, responsibly, with respect for people being
searched and without unlawful discrimination. Under the Equality Act 2010, section 149,
when police officers are carrying out their functions, they also have a duty to have due
regard to the need to eliminate unlawful discrimination, harassment and victimisation, to
advance equality of opportunity between people who share a ‘relevant protected
characteristic’ and people who do not share it, and to take steps to foster good relations
between those persons (see Notes 1 and 1A). The Children Act 2004, section 11, also
requires chief police officers and other specified persons and bodies to ensure that in the
discharge of their functions they have regard to the need to safeguard and promote the
welfare of all persons under the age of 18.
